title: Year 11 Investigating Science Module 3 – Scientific Models
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 11 Investigating Science Module 3. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

questions.prompt: What is a simplified representation of a scientific object, system or process called?
What type of model uses a labelled visual representation?
What type of model is a tangible three-dimensional copy or representation?
questions.answer: A physical replica. Accept: physical model.

questions.prompt: What type of model represents a system using numbers, equations or formulas?
questions.answer: A mathematical representation. Accept: mathematical model.

questions.prompt: What type of digital model imitates the behaviour of a real system?
Models often make complex scientific ideas easier to do what?
What can a model make about an outcome that has not yet been observed?
Models can be useful when a real process takes too long because of its what?
Models can replace some real-world testing when an investigation would be too expensive because of what factor?
Models can help scientists test new what before direct evidence is available?
What type of model can predict the spread of an infectious disease?
What type of model represents the structure of atoms?
What type of model is used to investigate changes in Earth’s climate?
What broad model type is used to represent the structure or development of the cosmos?
What type of model explains an unfamiliar idea by comparing it with something familiar?
What do all scientific models have because they cannot perfectly represent reality?
What can scientists do to a model when new evidence improves it without discarding it?
What may happen to a model if strong new evidence shows it is no longer suitable?
questions.answer: It may be replaced. Accept: contested or replaced.

questions.prompt: Which is generally easier to understand quickly: a simple model or a complex model?
Which type of model can usually represent more variables and detail: simple or complex?
What published scientific information should be consulted when planning a model?
A model should use resources that are what for the concept being represented?
After constructing a model, students should demonstrate how it can make what?
Whose feedback should be used when presenting and evaluating a constructed scientific model?
What formal process allows the scientific community to evaluate the accuracy and applicability of models?

finalRound.prompt: What is the main reason a scientific model may be refined or replaced over time?
finalRound.answer: New evidence. Accept: new scientific evidence or data.
